lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: transportation and appointment plan

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic transportation and appointment plan task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner names one real or realistic near-future need that requires getting somewhere at a specific time, such as a medical or dental appointment, a school event, or an activity, and writes a complete plan covering how they would get there, what it would cost, what they would need to bring, and what they would do when they arrive, without contacting or scheduling with any real outside person or office as part of this lesson.
safetyNotes: This plan is prepared as a real-world-ready document; it does not require contacting, confirming, or scheduling with any real outside person or office as part of this lesson.
materials: adult-or-local: information about the transportation options actually available to the household (walking distance, a transit schedule, or a trusted adult's availability)

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one specific way this transportation plan depends on a skill from a different system this year, such as a planning or communication skill.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u06-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Plan completeness across the four elements: Plan includes a specific, actionable route, an estimated cost, a document or item list, and a check-in description for the named need. | Backup-step realism: Backup step directly addresses the specific disruption named and is concrete enough to act on. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write a second plan for the same need using a different transportation mode, then compare the cost and time tradeoffs between the two plans in one paragraph.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic transportation and appointment plan task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: information about the transportation options actually available to the household (walking distance, a transit schedule, or a trusted adult's availability)
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: the learner's Unit 4 notes
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: transportation and appointment plan worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner names one real or realistic near-future need that requires getting somewhere at a specific time, such as a medical or dental appointment, a school event, or an activity, and writes a complete plan covering how they would get there, what it would cost, what they would need to bring, and what they would do when they arrive, without contacting or scheduling with any real outside person or office as part of this lesson.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact transportation and appointment plan decision or action.
Model move 2: Name one real or realistic near-future need that requires getting somewhere at a specific time.
Model move 3: Build your plan across all four elements: the route, the estimated cost, the needed documents or items, and the check-in step.

Model check: Plan completeness across the four elements: Plan includes a specific, actionable route, an estimated cost, a document or item list, and a check-in description for the named need. | Backup-step realism: Backup step directly addresses the specific disruption named and is concrete enough to act on.

resources.title: transportation and appointment plan action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for transportation and appointment plan.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: transportation and appointment plan coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner names one real or realistic near-future need that requires getting somewhere at a specific time, such as a medical or dental appointment, a school event, or an activity, and writes a complete plan covering how they would get there, what it would cost, what they would need to bring, and what they would do when they arrive, without contacting or scheduling with any real outside person or office as part of this lesson.
Coach direction: Name one real or realistic near-future need that requires getting somewhere at a specific time.
Learner prompt: Describe the need, including the type of appointment or event, and roughly when it would happen.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: transportation and appointment plan complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Build your plan across all four elements: the route, the estimated cost, the needed documents or items, and the check-in step.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My plan names the specific transportation mode and the route steps in order, with approximate times.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My plan includes an estimated cost for the trip, based on a published fare or a typical cost, if any.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My plan lists every document or item I would need to bring.
Response 4 (t2-p4): My plan describes exactly what I would do or say when I check in or arrive.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: transportation and appointment plan minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one specific way this transportation plan depends on a skill from a different system this year, such as a planning or communication skill.

Success checks: Plan completeness across the four elements: Plan includes a specific, actionable route, an estimated cost, a document or item list, and a check-in description for the named need. | Backup-step realism: Backup step directly addresses the specific disruption named and is concrete enough to act on.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: transportation and appointment plan supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u06-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional transportation and appointment plan condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Plan completeness across the four elements: Plan includes a specific, actionable route, an estimated cost, a document or item list, and a check-in description for the named need. | Backup-step realism: Backup step directly addresses the specific disruption named and is concrete enough to act on..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u06-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: transportation and appointment plan — complete fictional route

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
